### MAP-43A7CB72EF

- mapping source: [src/services/uta-supervisor/health.ts:9-13](../../../../src/services/uta-supervisor/health.ts#L9-L13)
- symbol: HealthBody wire shape
- id: MAP-43A7CB72EF
- sourceEvidence:
  - src/services/uta-supervisor/health.ts:9-13: HealthBody is a compile-time interface with ok:boolean, startedAt:string, and utas:number
- currentBehavior: The interface permits ok=false, arbitrary strings for startedAt, and any JavaScript number for utas. It is local to the supervisor module and is not a runtime-checked protocol type; decodeUTAHealth later narrows it only partially.
- problem: Alice and UTA do not share one wire schema, so producer and consumers can silently disagree. Raw timestamps cannot safely prove a process replacement, and NaN, Infinity, fractions, or negative counts can cross the boundary even though the status response represents a count.
- preservedBehavior:
  - The public health endpoint still reports process start time and the number of configured UTA instances; the ambiguous boolean is intentionally replaced by mandatory RuntimeHealth phase handling.
  - A process that successfully reaches the health handler is still distinguishable from an unreachable process, while Initializing/Recovering/Stopping/Failed are not treated as Ready.
  - No broker-health or execution-permission claim is added to the process response; unsupported native connection guarantees are not broadened.

### MAP-505C4A4F7D

- sourceEvidence:
  - src/services/uta-supervisor/restart-trigger.ts:66-70: mkdir(recursive), fixed .tmp sibling write in UTF-8, and rename to restart-uta.flag are used as the atomic Guardian signal
  - scripts/guardian/shared.ts:540-627, scripts/guardian/dev.ts:420-447, scripts/guardian/prod.mjs:481-532,567-592: current dev/prod launchers watch and debounce the flag but emit no structured request acknowledgement
  - packages/guardian-runtime/src/control-server.ts:42-165: an existing finite JSON-line Guardian control protocol is available for the restart method/status extension
- currentBehavior: The control directory is created as needed, a timestamp is written to a fixed temporary filename, and rename over the flag is the only acknowledgement visible to Alice. Concurrent callers contend on that path, the payload has no request identity, and the two launchers own separate file-watch behavior rather than a shared request/result contract.
- problem: Atomic visibility is not end-to-end acknowledgement. A fixed temp path and bare timestamp cannot express coalescing, owner continuity, or completion, and preserving the flag as a compatibility channel would leave two restart authorities with divergent semantics. Rename must not be treated as durable trading state or as proof of readiness.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Guardian remains responsible for whole-process SIGTERM, wait, escalation, respawn, and the existing bounded debounce policy.
  - Concurrent configuration changes can be coalesced without making a file rename look like readiness.

### MAP-A630EBD86C

- mapping source: [src/services/uta-supervisor/restart-trigger.ts:1-11](../../../../src/services/uta-supervisor/restart-trigger.ts#L1-L11)
- symbol: Guardian restart protocol documentation
- id: MAP-A630EBD86C
- sourceEvidence:
  - src/services/uta-supervisor/restart-trigger.ts:1-11: comments define an Alice-to-Guardian flag, Guardian SIGTERM/respawn, and a health wait based on a newer startedAt
  - packages/guardian-runtime/src/control-server.ts:42-165: existing finite Guardian control protocol accepts request ids and currently exposes runtime.status/runtime.stop; Unix sockets are chmod 0600 at lines 145-148
- currentBehavior: The documented protocol is a host process-control handshake: Alice writes a flag, Guardian notices it after debounce, restarts the whole UTA process with boot-time configuration, and Alice probes readiness. It is not a trading transaction and has no account-level restart claim. The existing control server is the only supported protocol extension point; current dev/prod flag watchers do not return a request-correlated result.
- problem: The comments describe an ordering and acknowledgement protocol but the implementation has only a file rename and a best-effort health comparison. There is no request identity, Guardian acceptance/completion signal, or durable distinction between process exit and new-process readiness. A later healthy response or changed display timestamp can therefore be attributed to the wrong request.
- preservedBehavior:
  - Alice remains up while Guardian restarts UTA, and trading requests can be unavailable during the gap.
  - The default operation is a full UTA respawn that rereads boot-time configuration.
  - Normal broker connection recovery remains distinct from process replacement.

### MAP-B9DC6715CE

- currentBehavior: The comment establishes a process-readiness concern, not a broker command: Alice and Guardian may probe UTA, and a missing result is treated as compatible with a carrier-less boot.
